result.title: Weight Scale Rebalancing: Transferable Training Recipes for Transformers
result.summary: Training Transformers requires careful hyperparameter tuning, which becomes increasingly costly for large models. We introduce UDV-Rebalance (UDVR), a reparameterization that inserts an auxiliary diagonal matrix $D$ between naturally paired weight matrices $(U,V)$ appearing throughout Transformer architectures. UDVR periodically rebalances the factors to maintain unit-norm columns in $U$ and unit-norm rows in $V$, with $D$ absorbing the corresponding scales. With rebalancing, a single hyperparameter setting of UDVR remains effective across model scales, architectures, and data distributions. This yields a tuning-free rule that adapts to each weight matrix using only its dimensions. We fit this rule once on ViT models trained on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and it remains valid when the activation function or the optimizer is changed. The same rule transfers to new image domains in DomainNet, to ViT, Swin, and MaxViT on ImageNet, and to language-model pretraining with up to 1.3B parameters. UDVR consistently outperforms Weight Normalization and $σ$Reparam and matches a vanilla baseline whose hyperparameters are swept on each target model.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 UDVR 重参数化：在成对权重矩阵间插入对角矩阵并周期性重平衡，使单一超参设定可跨模型规模、架构与数据分布迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作是通用 Transformer 训练超参迁移与权重尺度归一化技巧，不涉及视觉证据、latent 状态生成、停止决策或推理期计算分配，与 LVR 主线缺少可核查的具体联系。
